title: Netflix Q3 Earnings Beat on Profit, but Softer Guidance Hits the Stock
excerpt: Revenue of $12.87 billion and a 34.6 percent operating margin top the quarter; outlook and ad forecast disappoint.
body:
Netflix reported third-quarter 2026 results after the market close on October 20 that beat expectations on profit while disappointing investors on guidance. Revenue rose about 12 percent year over year to $12.87 billion, in line with both the company's forecast and Wall Street estimates, driven by membership growth, price increases and a growing advertising business. Diluted earnings per share reached $0.87, ahead of the $0.82 consensus, and net income climbed 44 percent to $3.66 billion.

Profitability was the standout. Operating income rose 37 percent to $4.46 billion and the operating margin widened to 34.6 percent from 28.2 percent a year earlier, helped by the timing of some expenses. Free cash flow totaled about $2.9 billion. Regionally, revenue grew 11 percent in the United States and Canada to $5.63 billion, 11 percent in EMEA, 17 percent in Latin America and 12 percent in Asia-Pacific.

The outlook is where the report stumbled. Netflix guided fourth-quarter revenue to $13.44 billion with EPS of $0.67, below expectations, and a 26 percent operating margin weighed down by costs from roughly 1,000 layoffs. It also narrowed full-year revenue guidance to about $51.1 billion and cut its 2026 advertising revenue outlook to about $2.7 billion from roughly $3.0 billion, citing a slower rollout of ad products. Shares fell about 5 percent in after-hours trading.
